stem.text: A nitrogen molecule P travelling at a speed of $320\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ in a vacuum collides with a stationary nitrogen molecule Q.
After the collision, P travels at a velocity of $180\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ at an angle of $55^{\circ}$ to its original path.
Q travels in a direction at an angle of $34^{\circ}$ to the initial path of P.

stem.alt: Circle labelled P with a horizontal arrow labelled 320 m s-1 pointing towards a circle labelled Q on a dashed horizontal line; captioned before collision.

Circle labelled P with an arrow labelled 180 m s-1 pointing up and to the right; circle labelled Q with an arrow labelled v pointing down and to the right; angles 55° and 34° marked from dashed lines; captioned after collision.

stem.text: Assume that there are no external forces acting on the molecules.
What is the magnitude $v$ of the velocity of Q after the collision?
